SECTION: GOOGLE WORKSPACE AT LSPU-LB (SCHOOL GOOGLE ACCOUNT)
GOOGLE WORKSPACE AT LSPU-LB (SCHOOL GOOGLE ACCOUNT)
Source: information from the project team and the maintainer that LSPU-LB mainly uses Google Workspace for study. The Student Handbook and Citizen's Charter do not describe it, except the Google Form used in Student ID processing (Citizen's Charter 2026, Business Affairs, Service 1, p. 13) and the Handbook's plan to use Google Classroom as the learning platform. Confirm the exact tools enabled and the account format with the university ICT office.
Google Workspace is Google's suite of online tools (Gmail, Classroom, Meet, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Calendar). It is mainly used at LSPU-LB for school-related activities: official school email, online classes and meetings, sharing and submitting coursework, group projects, forms and surveys, and schedules. Students use their school Google account to access these tools.
Account requirement: a school-issued Google account. Students request it inside the LSPU Student Portal once their portal account is active. The exact account format is not documented.
Because it is requested through the portal, activate your portal account first at the ICT office inside the CCS building.

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_821
SECTION: GOOGLE WORKSPACE FUNCTIONS: WHAT EACH TOOL IS USED FOR
GOOGLE WORKSPACE FUNCTIONS: WHAT EACH TOOL IS USED FOR
Source: general description of each Google tool and how the campus mainly uses it (maintainer and project team, September 2026).
- Google Classroom (online class management): join a class with a class code, read posted lessons and announcements, receive assignments, and submit outputs online.
- Google Meet (online meetings and classes): attend online lectures, consultations, and group meetings by video call.
- Gmail (school email): receive announcements from teachers, offices, and the college, and send school-related messages using the school Google account.
- Google Calendar (schedules and reminders): keep track of class schedules, deadlines, and school events, and receive reminders.
- Google Drive, Docs, Sheets and Slides (file storage and collaborative documents): store files in the cloud and write reports, spreadsheets, and presentations, alone or with groupmates, with shared editing.
- Google Forms (forms and surveys): fill out online forms, quizzes, surveys, and registrations. Example cited in the Citizen's Charter: Student ID processing starts by scanning a QR code or filling out a Google Form.

SOURCE: LSPU_SOURCE.txt | CHUNK: pillar3_txt_chunk_635
SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 3. LSPU Flexible Learning Delivery
learning competencies lifted from the OBE course syllabus that the teacher wishes students to perform after finishing the learning course or unit.

Student Learning Strategies. Flexible learning is self-paced and selfdirected, the IMs to be produced shall characterize as personalized learning by using it as a tool to adapt to student capabilities. The teacher determines the approach for achieving the learning objectives and are included in the pre-instructional activities, and lesson presentation adopting flexible learning options.

Performance Tasks. These are the activities that require the learners to perform the task or activity to standards. It will give students an experience for engagement attuned to the community of practice.

Understanding directed assessment. Assessment is done through faculty marked exams, portfolios, reflective/synthesis papers, research papers, projects, and innovative tools, among others.

Step 5. Google Classroom will be institutionalized as primary LSPU LMS platform and parameters on its use to support course delivery will be made available to faculty.

Sec. 4.

SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 3. LSPU Flexible Learning Delivery
Step 5. Google Classroom will be institutionalized as primary LSPU LMS platform and parameters on its use to support course delivery will be made available to faculty.

Sec. 4. Modified Grading Policy The Modified Grading Policy During the pandemic, shall be observed:

4.1. The university will continue using the numerical grading system for all students;

4.2. In preparation for the non-face-to-face conduct of teaching and learning, the university shall still adopt the grading system stated in the Student Handbook.

4.3. The bases for the computation of grades used in the grading system for each grading period may include quizzes, recitation/ participation, course requirements, activity sheets/projects. However, the New Normal permits the academic community to modify each grade. Hence, based on the online Self-paced Learning Module, the following components for the computation of grades shall be adopted:

4.3.1. Synchronous/Asynchronous: Course discussion – 20%; Activities/Performance Task 40% Final Exam /Outputs – 40%

4.3.2.
